speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Government has received any information from platform workers about delayed or missing CPF contributions when they join a new platform operator; and (b) if so, whether the Ministry will consider reviewing its operational processes and introduce measures to ensure that CPF contributions are properly made.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We will continue to monitor the timeliness and accuracy of CPF contributions made by platform operators and work closely with our tripartite partners to ensure platform operators' interests are always protected.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I declare that I am the advisor to the Platform Work Associations of the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC).

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We are grateful that the Government had taken into account, with the passing of the Platform Workers Bill, our platform workers' feedback on the need for retirement adequacy through fair platform worker contributions to CPF.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I, too, appreciate that the roll-out process for CPF is a complex one, given the difference in work conditions between a full-time employee receiving one monthly set of wages from one employer, to that of a platform worker receiving multiple sets of daily or even weekly wages due to the multi-homing nature of platform work.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I appreciate that the Ministry recognises this gap and is remedying the current operational processes.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In recognising this gap, will the Ministry, too, also consider introducing measures to mandate CPF contributions from their first month of work and to provide joint back payments with platform operators to those affected platform workers who had missed out on their rightful CPF contributions for their work done?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And given different join dates and opt-in statuses, platform operators will need some lead time to query the opt-in information, update their database and update their contribution rates in their system accordingly.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: This also means that if an opt-in platform worker onboard a new platform operator on 16 February, that platform operator will apply the higher CPF contribution rate from 1 April.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: All earnings payable from 16 February to 31 March would continue to attract CPF contributions at the non-opt-in rate.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: This payment does not constitute the delayed CPF contributions as the cut-off date, which is the 15th of the month, is currently legislated under the Fourth Schedule of the CPF Act.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: However, we assessed that this might not be favourable for the platform workers who experience inconsistent monthly earnings.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Those who do not set aside enough cash savings might find themselves cash strapped when platform workers deduct the platform workers' share of the CPF contributions from their back pay.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: In doing so, it is important to strike a balance between the platform workers' interest and what is practical for the platform operators to administer, as any arrangement must ultimately be workable in practice.
